title: The deploy engine: build at the landed sha, replace atomically, probe health, keep the previous receipt
description:
SPIDR child of task-04b3ce7e349743c2a156d32ee5550ba5 (architect-fa3a3e17, 2026-09-05), which measured over the file cap. dependsOn task-3706b7e7bb8741d88105f42c25166ea0 for the infrastructure files it builds from.

WHY THIS ROW EXISTS. The parent publishes TWO command kinds (`deployment.set_target`, `deployment.deploy`) AND owns the deploy effect. Publishing one command kind on this board is measured at 13 forced edits; two is more, and the engine is another eight files. This row is the dependency LEAF: the whole deploy effect as a pure, injectable, OFFLINE-testable service. NO command kind, NO vocabulary edit, NO registry edit, NO roster backfill - all of that is the parent.

MEASURED AT HEAD (branch moe/work-2026-09-04) by architect-fa3a3e17:
- `git grep -c "deployment\\.deploy|deployment\\.set_target" -- apps packages tests` = 0. No deployment surface exists. The gap is real.
- THE PATTERN TO MIRROR IS `repository.publish`, and it is small: `apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/node-publisher.ts` is 77 lines (`NodePublisherConfig:20`, `PublishReport:29`, `createNodePublisher:35`) - a thin effect runner, not a framework.
- THE RECEIPT SHAPE IS `apps/daemon/src/repository/publish-receipt-contracts.ts`: `PUBLISH_RECEIPT_VERSION = "moe-publish-receipt/1"` (:16), `PUBLISH_RECEIPT_COMMAND_KIND = "internal.repository.publish_receipt"` (:17), `PublishRefusal` (:36), `PublishReceiptV1` (:41), and a decode-result union (:57). Mirror it.
- INTERNAL RECEIPT KINDS NEED NO ROSTER BACKFILL. `grep -n "internal\\." apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-vocabulary.ts` returns ZERO - `internal.*` receipt kinds are outside PAYLOAD_KEYS, the registry and the MCP roster entirely. That is what lets this row own `moe-deploy-receipt/1` without touching a roster. Confirm it before writing the receipt; if it has changed, STOP rather than absorbing a backfill.

THE PREVIOUS RECEIPT'S SHAPE IS THIS ROW'S MOST CONSEQUENTIAL OUTPUT. The monitoring/rollback row (task-7683a432eb3f4e87b1eb0cbc6e3a55ff) rolls back to it and is a SIBLING that cannot depend on this row - so it will build against whatever ships. Get the shape right the first time.

ATOMIC REPLACE IS THE PROPERTY THAT MATTERS. A deploy that stops the old container before the new one is healthy produces a window where the product is down and the operator sees an outage they did not cause.
definitionOfDone: The deploy effect is tested OFFLINE through injectable docker/ssh ports that capture argv, asserting the ARGV BYTE-FOR-BYTE: the build tag EQUALS the landed sha, and the ssh path is `docker save | ssh docker load`. A tag that is not the sha makes every later rollback, dossier and incident claim unverifiable, so assert the tag against the sha value rather than against a pattern. No test may reach the network or a real docker daemon.

ATOMIC REPLACE PROVEN, not asserted in prose: through the port's recorded call ORDER, assert the OLD container still serves until the NEW one answers health, and that there is NO point in the sequence at which neither serves. Mutate the service to a stop-then-start order and confirm the arm goes RED - an ordering property that has never been seen red is not evidence.

DEPLOY_HEALTH_TIMEOUT REFUSES and leaves the environment in a DEFINED state - the old container still running - asserted with code AND layer, and asserted by reading the port's final state rather than by trusting the return value. A half-deployed environment reporting success is worse than a refusal.

DEPLOY_TARGET_MISSING, DEPLOY_BUILD_FAILED and DEPLOY_DOCKER_UNAVAILABLE each assert code AND layer. DEPLOY_BUILD_FAILED carries the tool's ACTUAL last stderr line, not a generic message - assert the real stderr text reaches the refusal, since a generic build failure is undiagnosable from a receipt.

`moe-deploy-receipt/1` records {environment, sha, imageDigest, url, DEPLOYED|REFUSED(code)}, mirroring apps/daemon/src/repository/publish-receipt-contracts.ts including its null-pairing discipline (exactly one of the success member and the refusal member populated). A REFUSED receipt carries its code and no imageDigest, asserted as its own arm.

THE PREVIOUS RECEIPT IS KEPT AND READABLE: assert that two successive deploys leave BOTH receipts retrievable and distinguishable by sha. The rollback row task-7683a432eb3f4e87b1eb0cbc6e3a55ff is a sibling that cannot depend on this one and will build against this shape, so document the retrieval call it should use in the completion record.

A PRODUCTION deploy CITES the release decision when one exists on the goal and states 'no release decision' when none does - assert BOTH wordings. It neither invents an approval nor refuses for lack of one. The decision is read through an injectable port; this row does not implement Gate 3 (task-2a345b2e97d94599b4688af1923056e5, a sibling).

EVERY container, temp directory and child process the tests create is released on EVERY exit path including the throwing one (epic rail 4) - teardown in a `finally`, not after the assertions. Invoke `docker`/`ssh` as bare executables under shell:false with argv arrays; never a hard-coded `.cmd`, never a shell string, never a chain. Gates quoted with their `Test Files N passed` count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm typecheck`.
taskRails: NO COMMAND KIND. No edit to daemon-command-vocabulary.ts, daemon-command-registry.ts, mcp-tool-allowlist.ts, agent-spawn-contract.ts or packages/contracts - every one belongs to the parent task-04b3ce7e349743c2a156d32ee5550ba5 and touching them here collides in the shared worktree.
ATOMIC REPLACE: the old container serves until the new one is healthy. A stop-then-start deploy is an outage the operator did not ask for.
THE IMAGE TAG IS THE LANDED SHA. Every later claim - rollback, dossier, incident - resolves through it.
KEEP THE PREVIOUS RECEIPT and get its shape right first time: the rollback row is a SIBLING that cannot depend on this row, so it will build against whatever ships.
FOLLOW `repository.publish`'s pattern (node-publisher.ts, publish-receipt-contracts.ts). A second deployment shape is a second thing to reason about during an incident.
OFFLINE TESTS ONLY. Every port is injectable; no test may reach the network or a real docker daemon. A test that leaks a container or a port makes every later gate on this board inadmissible.

implementationPlan.description: MEASURE AND BASELINE. NO EDITS — this step deliberately declares no affected files. The stop question that halted the previous attempt is SETTLED; do not re-litigate it. DoD-2 has been ruled out of this row and moved verbatim to task-db63dacc7cbe49cab9826e9b49c8669f, which dependsOn this row; read comment-0c8df7d157464e338b11dfe81d0bcd02 for the ruling before anything else. YOU BUILD SEVEN OF THE EIGHT DoD ITEMS: 1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8. You do NOT build the atomic flip, you do NOT touch deployment-infrastructure-templates.ts, and you do NOT describe anything here as atomic. (a) RE-CONFIRM THE TWO STOP CONDITIONS, both directions of global rail 19, and STOP if either has moved. `grep -c 'internal\.' apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-vocabulary.ts` must still be 0 — that is what keeps `internal.deployment.deploy_receipt` outside PAYLOAD_KEYS, the registry and the MCP roster, so this row owes NO roster backfill. `ls apps/daemon/src/deployment` must still be absent and `git grep -l -E 'DEPLOY_HEALTH_TIMEOUT|moe-deploy-receipt|DEPLOY_TARGET_MISSING' -- apps packages adapters tests tools` must still return nothing; if a peer has landed any of it, STOP rather than shipping a silent duplicate. Note that `git grep -c -E 'deployment\.deploy|deployment\.set_target'` is NO LONGER zero — task-44760ed1 is DONE and published the kinds. That is the parent's job done, NOT a roster job arriving here; it changes nothing for you. (b) READ THE FOUR MIRRORS (paths in planningNotes.keyFiles), all small and all deliberate: `orchestrator/node-publisher.ts` (77 lines — a thin effect runner whose header states the discipline: 'Nothing here chooses a remote, a branch, or a moment'); `repository/publish-receipt-contracts.ts` (185 — `PublishRefusal {code, detail}`:36, `PublishReceiptV1`:41 with the null-pairing shape, decode union :57, anchored `HEX64`/`GIT_OBJECT_ID`, exact `RECEIPT_KEYS`/`REFUSAL_KEYS`); `repository/publish-ledger.ts` (246 — `readPublishLedger`:88 paging `store.readCommandDecisionsAfter`, `readPublishReceipt`:174, `recordPublishReceipt`:199 which computes a deterministic receiptId, reads it back FIRST and returns `{ok:true, receipt, replayed:true}` on a repeat — copy that idempotence); `repository/git-landing-port.ts` (250 — `GitRunner = (cwd, args, stdin?) => Promise<{code, stderr, stdout}>`:68, `GIT_TIMEOUT_MS`/`MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES`/`DETAIL_TAIL` at :72-74, refusals carrying git's own words in `detail`). (c) READ THE HEALTHCHECK YOU WILL PROBE. `repository/deployment/deployment-infrastructure-templates.ts:89` generates `HEALTHCHECK --interval=5s --timeout=5s --start-period=5s --retries=20`; `:146` repeats it in the compose service. Compute the worst case yourself and record it: 5s start-period + 20 x 5s = 105s before DOCKER ITSELF reports `unhealthy`. Your budget must EXCEED that or the engine refuses before docker has decided anything — that is the derivation DoD-8's completion record asks for, and it is why 60s (git's number) would be wrong here. (d) BASELINE, standalone foreground, one command per call, quoting each count line: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm typecheck`. An exit-0 leg with no `Test Files N passed` line ran NOTHING. Root `pnpm test` is not evidence for any file in this row — vitest.config.ts includes no `apps/**`. (e) `git status --porcelain -- apps/daemon/src`; ~25 untracked peer files live there. Note them, never revert, stash or `git add -A`.

THE RECEIPT CONTRACT (DoD-5). NEW `apps/daemon/src/deployment/deploy-receipt-contracts.ts`, target <=250 lines (its mirror is 185). Mirror `publish-receipt-contracts.ts` in SHAPE by reading it, not by copy-paste. Declare `DEPLOY_RECEIPT_VERSION = "moe-deploy-receipt/1"`, `DEPLOY_RECEIPT_COMMAND_KIND = "internal.deployment.deploy_receipt"` (the `internal.*` prefix is the whole reason this row owes no roster backfill — step 1a), a reserved principal id beside the `NODE_PUBLISHER_PRINCIPAL_ID` precedent at :15, and the FOUR refusal codes `DEPLOY_TARGET_MISSING`, `DEPLOY_BUILD_FAILED`, `DEPLOY_DOCKER_UNAVAILABLE`, `DEPLOY_HEALTH_TIMEOUT`. THE LAYER STAMP IS A MEASURED TRAP, so name it deliberately: DoD-4 requires every refusal to carry code AND layer, but `tests/security/boundary-roster.security.ts:331` scans production sources with `/^export const ([A-Z_]+(?:LAYERS|LAYER|BOUNDARIES))\s*(?::[^=]+)?=/u`, and a column-zero exported const whose NAME ends in LAYER/LAYERS/BOUNDARIES is treated as a public security boundary owing a roster row plus overall/package/axis cardinality pins plus BEFORE/AFTER/RACE cases under `tests/security/` — foreign files that would blow this row's cap. Declare `export const DEPLOY_ENGINE_STAMP = "DAEMON_DEPLOY_ENGINE" as const;` and `export type DeployEngineStamp = typeof DEPLOY_ENGINE_STAMP;`. The VALUE may read DAEMON_DEPLOY_ENGINE; only the CONST NAME is scanned. Precedent: `DAEMON_FOUNDATION_ATTEMPT` (work/foundation-attempt-contracts.ts:36), `FOUNDATION_CONTEXT_CODEC`. Note the mirror carries NO layer at all, so this member is your addition rather than a copy: `DeployRefusal` is `{code, detail, layer}`. `DeployReceiptV1` carries {environment, sha, imageDigest, url, outcome} plus the record-keeping members its sibling carries (decidedAt, decisionId, projectId, receiptId, version). THE NULL-PAIRING DISCIPLINE IS THE POINT AND IT IS A VALIDATOR, NOT A TYPE: `PublishReceiptV1` pairs `outcome: "PUSHED"|"REFUSED"` against `sha|branch|url|refusal: T | null` with EXACTLY ONE side populated. `T | null` on both sides merely PERMITS the pairing; the discipline is a decoder that REFUSES both-populated and neither-populated. Carry it literally: a DEPLOYED receipt has an imageDigest and a NULL refusal; a REFUSED receipt has its code and a NULL imageDigest. Encode an exact-key decode (mirror `RECEIPT_KEYS`/`REFUSAL_KEYS`) returning `{ok:true, receipt} | {code:"DEPLOY_RECEIPT_INVALID", ok:false}`, and validate the sha with the same ANCHORED hex pattern its sibling uses for git object ids — a tag that is not a sha is the failure DoD-1 exists to prevent, and catching it at decode is cheaper than at rollback. ALSO CREATE the one-line ES bridge `deploy-receipt-contracts.js` containing exactly `export * from "./deploy-receipt-contracts.ts";` — every tracked sibling has one (measured: `repository/deployment/deployment-infrastructure-generator.js` is that single line, and publish-ledger, git-landing-port and node-publisher all have `.js` twins), and without it every `.js`-specifier import of this module fails to resolve.

THE PORTS AND THE STATE-MACHINE DOUBLE. NEW `apps/daemon/src/deployment/deploy-ports.ts` (+ its one-line `.js` bridge, same pattern as step 2), target <=250 lines. FOUR INJECTABLE PORTS, all following `GitRunner`'s shape at git-landing-port.ts:68 rather than inventing one: (i) `DockerRunner = (args: readonly string[], stdin?) => Promise<{code, stderr, stdout}>`; (ii) `SshRunner` of the same shape; (iii) a DEPLOY TARGET port answering the environment's target or null (DoD-4's `DEPLOY_TARGET_MISSING` reads it; the target is WRITTEN by the parent task-04b3ce7e's `deployment.set_target` — you only read, through the port); (iv) a RELEASE DECISION port answering the goal's decision or null (DoD-7; Gate 3 is task-2a345b2e, a sibling — implementing a gate here would be inventing authority). Pick your own timeout and output bounds and SAY WHY in the step note: git uses 60_000ms / 8MB / 600-char tail, but step 1(c) measured that docker's own healthcheck needs 105s before it will even say `unhealthy`, so the health budget must exceed that — take `DEPLOY_HEALTH_BUDGET_MS = 150_000` with a 2s poll (finer than docker's 5s interval, and cheap), and a separate longer build timeout. SPAWN DISCIPLINE IS A RAIL: bare executable `docker` / `ssh` under `shell: false` with an ARGV ARRAY — never a hard-coded `.cmd`, never a shell string, never a chain. `orchestrator/moe-up-spawn.ts:103-111` states `shell: false` explicitly rather than relying on the default and documents why ('a shell here would re-parse a store path containing spaces and silently run a different argv'); do the same, with your own reason. THE `docker save | ssh docker load` PIPE IS THE SUBTLE PART (DoD-1): a pipe is a SHELL construct and you have no shell. Join the two children's streams in Node — `save`'s stdout into `ssh`'s stdin — and surface BOTH children's failures, because a pipe hides the first process's exit code by default and `${PIPESTATUS[0]}` is the shell answer you do not have. Record in the step note exactly how you connected them and how each child's nonzero code reaches the refusal. NOW THE DOUBLE, and this is the design decision that decides whether the ordering properties are provable at all: A PURE ARGV RECORDER CANNOT ANSWER 'was there a point at which neither container served'. Recording calls in order tells you what was INVOKED, not what was RUNNING. So export a SMALL STATE-MACHINE double beside the port it doubles: it interprets the recorded argv and tracks each container as absent/starting/healthy/stopped/removed, and exposes both the ordered call log AND the resulting state for assertion. DoD-3 demands exactly this — 'asserted by reading the port's final state rather than by trusting the return value'. Export it as production-tier from this module, NOT from a test file: task-db63dacc7 (the flip row, gated behind this one) and task-da60dc4b39c both need to drive the same model of what docker did, and two models of that is two things to reason about during an incident.

THE LEDGER (DoD-6), and its retrieval call is a deliverable, not a detail. NEW `apps/daemon/src/deployment/deploy-ledger.ts` (+ its one-line `.js` bridge), target <=250 lines, mirroring `repository/publish-ledger.ts` (246). Export `recordDeployReceipt(store, input)` mirroring `recordPublishReceipt`:199 — deterministic receiptId, READ IT BACK FIRST, and return `{ok:true, receipt, replayed:true}` on a repeat rather than writing a second row; that idempotence is what makes the 'same sha deployed twice' case answerable instead of accidental. Export `readDeployLedger(store, projectId)` mirroring `readPublishLedger`:88, paging `store.readCommandDecisionsAfter(cursor, LEDGER_PAGE_SIZE)` and keyed BY ENVIRONMENT, holding for each environment the CURRENT receipt and the PREVIOUS one. THE PREVIOUS RECEIPT IS THIS ROW'S MOST CONSEQUENTIAL OUTPUT: task-da60dc4b39c (the rollback effect) is WORKING RIGHT NOW and CANNOT depend on this row, so it will build against whatever ships. Give the retrieval a name and a signature it can call without reading your implementation — `readPreviousDeployReceipt(store, projectId, environment): DeployReceiptV1 | null` — and keep it a thin, separately-exported function over `readDeployLedger` so a caller that only wants the rollback target does not have to understand the ledger. DoD-6 asks you to NAME this call with its signature in the completion record; treat that as the interface publication it is. Keeping the previous receipt means BOTH stay retrievable and distinguishable by sha: do not overwrite, do not collapse, and do not key on sha alone (a redeploy of the same sha must not make the previous one unreachable).

THE ENGINE (DoD-1, 3, 4, 7). NEW `apps/daemon/src/deployment/deploy-service.ts` (+ its one-line `.js` bridge), target <=250 lines. `node-publisher.ts` is 77 lines and the rail says follow it: a THIN effect runner, not a framework. Nothing here chooses a moment or a policy — the caller names the environment and the sha, the ports do the work, one receipt is recorded per deploy. THE SEQUENCE: resolve the target through the target port (absent -> `DEPLOY_TARGET_MISSING`); confirm docker answers at all (a spawn ENOENT or a failing `docker version` -> `DEPLOY_DOCKER_UNAVAILABLE`); BUILD the image tagged with the LANDED SHA — DoD-1 says the tag EQUALS the sha VALUE, not a pattern that matches one, because every later rollback, dossier and incident claim resolves through that tag; transfer it when the target is remote via the Node-joined `docker save | ssh docker load`; START THE CANDIDATE WITH NO PUBLISHED HOST PORT — internal only, on the compose network, under a deterministic container name derived from environment and sha that tolerates the same sha being deployed twice (a name collision must be handled, not crashed on); PROBE THE CANDIDATE SPECIFICALLY with `docker inspect --format {{.State.Health.Status}} <candidateName>` polled until `healthy` or the budget expires. THAT ARGV NAMES THE CANDIDATE, AND THAT IS THE POINT: a probe addressed at the environment's public url would answer 200 from the OLD container and every deploy would 'pass' health instantly — the subtlest bug available in this row, killed structurally rather than by discipline. FOUR REFUSALS, EACH CARRYING CODE AND LAYER (DoD-4), the layer being step 2's `DEPLOY_ENGINE_STAMP`. `DEPLOY_BUILD_FAILED` CARRIES THE TOOL'S ACTUAL LAST STDERR LINE, not a generic message — `git-landing-port.ts` clips git's own words into `detail` with `DETAIL_TAIL` for the same reason: a generic build failure is undiagnosable from a receipt weeks later. ON `DEPLOY_HEALTH_TIMEOUT` THE OLD CONTAINER KEEPS RUNNING AND THE CANDIDATE IS REMOVED (DoD-3): a refusal must leave a DEFINED state, and the tidy-up of the failed candidate belongs on the FAILURE PATH IN A `finally`, not after the happy path. A half-deployed environment reporting success is worse than a refusal — and so is one reporting a refusal while leaking a stray container. THE RELEASE-DECISION READ (DoD-7) IS A PORT READ AND NOTHING MORE: for a PRODUCTION deploy, cite the decision when the port answers one and state 'no release decision' when it does not; it neither invents an approval nor refuses for the lack of one. Record exactly one receipt per deploy through step 4's `recordDeployReceipt`. THIS ROW STOPS AT A HEALTHY CANDIDATE AND A RECORDED RECEIPT. It does NOT flip traffic and does NOT stop the incumbent on the success path — that is task-db63dacc7cbe49cab9826e9b49c8669f, which dependsOn this row. Leave the seam where the flip will attach (the point after health and before any incumbent teardown) and SAY SO in a comment; do not stub it, do not name the result atomic anywhere in code, comment, test name or step note.

THE TESTS, OFFLINE. Two new files beside their modules. NO TEST MAY REACH THE NETWORK OR A REAL DOCKER DAEMON (task rail 6) — every port is step 3's double. In `deploy-receipt-contracts.test.ts` (DoD-5): a DEPLOYED receipt round-trips through encode/decode with an imageDigest and a NULL refusal; a REFUSED receipt round-trips carrying its code and a NULL imageDigest; and — the arm that makes the discipline real — a HAND-BUILT receipt with BOTH the imageDigest and the refusal populated is REFUSED by the decoder with `DEPLOY_RECEIPT_INVALID`, and so is one with NEITHER. Without those last two the shape merely permits nulls on both sides, which is the absence of a discipline rather than one. Also assert an unanchored-looking sha (right length, wrong alphabet; and a valid-hex string of the wrong length) is refused at decode. In `deploy-service.test.ts`: (1) DoD-1 — the build argv asserted BYTE-FOR-BYTE with the tag EQUAL to the sha VALUE bound in the test, never `toMatch(/[0-9a-f]{40}/)`, which passes for the WRONG sha; and both argv arrays of the `save | ssh load` path asserted INDEPENDENTLY, plus an arm where the FIRST child fails and the refusal still carries its stderr (the exit code a shell pipe would have swallowed). (2) DoD-3 — health budget expires, the refusal carries `DEPLOY_HEALTH_TIMEOUT` AND the layer, and the double's FINAL STATE shows the old container still running and the candidate REMOVED; assert the state, not the return value. (3) DoD-4 — `DEPLOY_TARGET_MISSING` and `DEPLOY_DOCKER_UNAVAILABLE` each with code AND layer, and `DEPLOY_BUILD_FAILED` carrying a DISTINCTIVE stderr string planted in the double, asserted as that exact text reaching the refusal so a generic message cannot pass. (4) DoD-6 — two successive deploys with DIFFERENT shas leave BOTH receipts retrievable through `readPreviousDeployReceipt` and distinguishable BY SHA; plus a third arm where the SAME sha is deployed twice and the ledger replays rather than losing the previous entry. (5) DoD-7 — both wordings asserted: a production deploy CITING a release decision the port answers, and one STATING 'no release decision' when the port answers null, and neither refuses. (6) THE PROBE-ADDRESSING ARM, which no DoD names but which the risks section calls the subtlest bug here: seed the double with an OLD container reporting healthy and a candidate reporting `starting`, and assert the deploy does NOT succeed — proving the probe reads the candidate and not the thing it is replacing. (7) EPIC RAIL 4 APPLIES TO THE TESTS THEMSELVES: every temp directory, store handle and child the tests create is released on EVERY exit path INCLUDING THE THROWING ONE — teardown in `finally`, never after the assertions. A test that leaks makes every later gate on this board inadmissible.

DRILLS, GATES, SELF-REVIEW, COMPLETION RECORD. (a) DRILLS, recorded verbatim in the step note. `git status --porcelain` THE EXACT MUTATED PATHS FIRST. EVERY FILE THIS ROW CREATES IS NEW AND UNTRACKED (`??`), so global rail 13 fires in full: `git diff` is BLIND to all of them — empty before, during and after — and a silently-unrestored mutation would ride into the commit wearing a clean diff with its arms green because the mutation is what they were re-graded against. Back each mutated path up OUT OF TREE (%TEMP%, suffixed by your worker id) and prove restoration by SHA256 EQUALITY in a call SEPARATE from the restore; a PowerShell copy can silently no-op and 'the command returned' is not evidence the bytes moved. State that no tracked path was mutated. THREE DRILLS: (i) change the build tag from the sha to any other value and confirm the DoD-1 arm goes RED NAMING the expected sha — if it stays green the assertion was a pattern, not a value, and every rollback that resolves through that tag is unverifiable; (ii) populate BOTH the imageDigest and the refusal on one receipt and confirm the decoder refuses — if it passes, the null-pairing discipline was never encoded; (iii) make the health probe address the environment url instead of the candidate container name and confirm the probe-addressing arm goes RED — that is the drill for the bug that would make DoD-3 vacuous while green. (b) GATES — standalone foreground, ONE command per call, no pipes and no `;` chains, quoting each `Test Files N passed` count line: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, then `pnpm typecheck`. AN EXIT-0 LEG WITH NO COUNT LINE RAN NOTHING and calling it a pass is a false completion claim. Root `pnpm test` is NOT evidence for a single file in this row — vitest.config.ts includes no `apps/**`. Attribute red by failing paths at HEAD minus the step-1 baseline, intersected with this row's owned paths; that intersection must be EMPTY, and any foreign red is reported VERBATIM with its exact failing lines, never hidden and never fabricated green. (c) ADVERSARIAL PASS on this diff only: a candidate container NAME that collides when the same sha is deployed twice — crash, reuse, or refusal, and is that what the ledger's replay arm assumes; a `docker save` that fails AFTER `ssh` has already started — is the ssh child killed or left waiting on a stdin that never closes; an environment name or url carrying a shell metacharacter — you use no shell, so CONFIRM that is actually true of EVERY call site rather than of the one you remember writing; a receipt recorded before the candidate is cleaned up on the refusal path — which state does the receipt claim; any container, temp dir, store handle or child left alive on a THROWING path. (d) COMPLETION RECORD (2000-char cap; put counts, file lists and drill transcripts in a row comment under ~4500 chars each) MUST STATE: the exact retrieval call task-da60dc4b39c should use for the previous receipt WITH ITS FULL SIGNATURE — `readPreviousDeployReceipt(store, projectId, environment): DeployReceiptV1 | null` — since DoD-6 asks for it by name and that row cannot depend on this one; the health budget you chose and the 105s derivation (5s start-period + 20 x 5s retries, `deployment-infrastructure-templates.ts:89`) that makes git's 60s wrong here; how the `save | ssh load` streams were joined in Node and how EACH child's failure reaches the refusal; drill (i) verbatim; that DoD-2 was RULED OUT to task-db63dacc7cbe49cab9826e9b49c8669f rather than approximated, and that nothing in this diff claims atomicity; and that no command kind, vocabulary, registry, allowlist, contracts or infrastructure-template file was touched — `git status --porcelain` proves it. Report ALL TEN created paths in complete_step.modifiedFiles, the four `.js` bridges included.

STATE: the shipped infrastructure has NO switch point — docker-compose.override.yml (task-3706b7e7, DONE) runs one `app` service publishing `3000:3000` directly; base compose (task-4a0f7064, DONE) ships `db` only; zero proxy/`docker service`/`start-first` hits anywhere. A published host port is fixed at container create, so a candidate cannot start beside the incumbent and DoD-2's recorded atomic-replace call order is not executable; stop-then-start called atomic would be a fabrication (task rail 2). ARCHITECT RULING NEEDED, one of: (1) a prerequisite row adding a flippable upstream (proxy) in 3706b7e7's dockerComposeOverride, DoD-2 unchanged; (2) network-alias switch, DoD-2 amended to the internal service name; (3) DoD-2 amended to what the infrastructure backs, outage window named. TWO THINGS THIS ROW LEFT UNSETTLED THAT WOULD SURFACE MID-STEP. architect-b63fabf3, 2026-09-05, HEAD f3b94eaa. Plan approved: 6 steps, 6 files, all new.

Both of the row's measured claims re-confirmed at plan time: the deployment gap is real (`git grep -c` = 0), and `grep -c 'internal\.' daemon-command-vocabulary.ts` = **0**, so `internal.*` receipt kinds really are outside PAYLOAD_KEYS, the registry and the MCP roster. `moe-deploy-receipt/1` costs no backfill — same mechanism `SEAT_EXIT_COMMAND_KIND` uses.

## 1. DoD-2 may be unbuildable on what the sibling shipped

"Atomic replace" needs something *flippable*, and **bare docker gives you none** — you cannot re-publish a port on a running container. So "start new, probe health, flip" requires a reverse-proxy upstream, a compose service alias, or equivalent — and that switch point is defined by what **task-3706b7e7 generates**, not by this row.

Step 1 therefore makes the worker read what that row actually shipped *before* designing the flip, and makes "the generated infrastructure defines no switch point" a **stop-and-report** — with the compose file quoted. The two outcomes to refuse are shipping a stop-then-start deploy described as atomic, and inventing a proxy inside another row's generated files (rail 1 forbids reaching across).

## 2. An argv recorder cannot prove atomicity

DoD-2 asks whether there was *any point at which neither container served*. A recorder answers "what was invoked, in what order" — not what was **running**. So the test double must be a **small state machine** tracking each container as started/healthy/stopped. DoD-3 already implies it ("assert by reading the port's final state rather than by trusting the return value"); the plan makes it explicit and puts it beside the port, so the service tests and any later row share one model of what docker did.

And the arm must **walk every transition**, not check the endpoints: a stop-then-start deploy has correct endpoints and a hole in the middle — precisely what a naive arm misses.

## The subtlest bug available here, named in the adversarial pass

**A health probe that addresses the environment's public URL rather than the candidate container** answers 200 from the *old* container while the new one is still starting. Every deploy then "passes" health instantly, and DoD-2 and DoD-3 are both vacuous while green.

## Three smaller findings carried into the plan

- **The `docker save | ssh docker load` pipe is a shell construct and there is no shell.** The streams join in Node, and a pipe hides the first child's exit code by default — `${PIPESTATUS[0]}` is the shell answer and unavailable here. Both argv arrays asserted independently, both children's failures surfaced.
- **`toMatch(/[0-9a-f]{40}/)` passes for the wrong sha.** DoD-1 says the tag *equals* the sha value; every later rollback and incident claim resolves through it. Drill (ii) proves the assertion is a value, not a pattern.
- **Null-pairing is a validator, not a type.** `T | null` on both sides merely *permits* the pairing; the discipline is a decoder that refuses both-populated and neither-populated. Drill (iii) proves it was encoded.

## The output that outlives this row

DoD-6's retrieval call. `task-7683a432` (rollback) is a **sibling that cannot depend on this row** and will build against whatever ships — so the completion record must name the call and its signature, mirroring `readPublishLedger(store, projectId)` / `recordPublishReceipt`. That is a deliverable, not a formality.

=== (a) ROSTER CLAIM RE-CONFIRMED; GAP MOVED IN THE HARMLESS DIRECTION ===
`grep -c 'internal\.' apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-vocabulary.ts` = 0, UNCHANGED. `internal.*` receipt kinds remain outside PAYLOAD_KEYS, the registry and the MCP roster, so `moe-deploy-receipt/1` still costs no backfill. Step 1(a)'s stop condition is NOT tripped.

No deploy ENGINE exists: `git grep -l -E "DEPLOY_HEALTH_TIMEOUT|DEPLOY_BUILD_FAILED|moe-deploy-receipt|DEPLOY_TARGET_MISSING"` over apps packages adapters tests tools = ZERO hits, and `apps/daemon/src/deployment/` does not exist. Rail 19 both directions: the engine gap is real, nothing to duplicate.

=== (b) THE SWITCH POINT DOES NOT EXIST ===
Base `docker-compose.yml` (task-4a0f7064 DONE, controlled-profile-root-templates.ts:124 DOCKER_COMPOSE) contains services: `db` only - postgres:17-alpine publishing "5432:5432" plus the db-data volume. No app service, no proxy.
`docker-compose.override.yml` (task-3706b7e7 DONE, deployment-infrastructure-templates.ts dockerComposeOverride) contains ONE service, `app`, and it binds the public port DIRECTLY:
    "  app:"
    "    build:" / "      context: ." / "      dockerfile: Dockerfile"
    "    restart: unless-stopped"
    "    depends_on:" / "      db:" / "        condition: service_healthy"
    "    ports:"
    '      - "3000:3000"'
    "    healthcheck:" test ["CMD","node","/app/healthcheck.mjs"] interval 5s timeout 5s retries 20
Full-tree searches for an indirection: `git grep -in -E "nginx|traefik|caddy|reverse.?proxy|upstream" -- apps packages adapters tools` returns only unrelated refusal-code prose in apps/control-room (no infrastructure hit). `git grep -in -E "docker stack|update_config|start-first|docker service" -- apps packages` = ZERO. All 44 epic rows read from .moe/tasks: no row owns a proxy or an alias. Epic architectureNotes name no switch point either.

=== WHY THAT MAKES DoD-2 UNSATISFIABLE, NOT MERELY AWKWARD ===
DoD-2 requires the recorded call ORDER to show the old container still serving until the new one answers health. That order is not executable here. A published host port is fixed at container create time and cannot be re-published on a running container, and two containers cannot bind 0.0.0.0:3000 simultaneously ("port is already allocated"). So the engine cannot start the candidate alongside the incumbent on the app's public port, and there is no proxy upstream, network alias or swarm routing mesh to flip instead.
The two workarounds are both forbidden here and both are worse than a refusal: (i) ship stop-then-start and call it atomic - the fabrication task rail 2 and DoD-2 exist to prevent; (ii) give the candidate an ephemeral host port, probe it, then stop the incumbent and RE-CREATE the candidate on 3000 - the container that ends up taking traffic is then a different, never-probed container, which defeats DoD-3 as well.

=== WHAT AN ARCHITECT COULD RULE (this row owns none of these files) ===
1. Add a flippable upstream to task-3706b7e7's `dockerComposeOverride` (a proxy service publishing 3000, app unpublished) as a new prerequisite row; this row then flips the upstream and DoD-2 stands unchanged.
2. Rule the switch point to be a docker network alias, and amend DoD-2 to the internal service name rather than the public url - honest, but it does not close the public-url gap.
3. Amend DoD-2 to the property the shipped infrastructure CAN back, with the outage window named explicitly rather than described as atomic.

=== ORTHOGONAL AND SALVAGEABLE ===
Steps 2-3 (the `moe-deploy-receipt/1` contract with its null-pairing decode, and the injectable docker/ssh ports) do not depend on the switch ruling: DoD-5's members and DoD-4's four refusal codes are fixed by the DoD. The row description calls the receipt shape this row's most consequential output because the rollback row task-7683a432/task-da60dc4b cannot depend on this row. I did NOT land them speculatively - plan step 1(b) says STOP AND REPORT, and a half-built module with no consumer on a shared branch is the producer-without-a-consumer-edge anti-pattern. Say the word and they ship in one session.

=== BASELINE (step 1d/1e) ===
`pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck` -> exit 0, GREEN, execution proven by the `$ tsc --project tsconfig.json` script echo. The two foreign reds QA recorded on 2026-09-05 (preview-runner.test.ts TS2379, release-decide-contracts.test.ts TS5097) are gone. `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` NOT run: it did not finish in ~35 min for QA on this host, and with zero bytes delivered it is load-bearing for no claim I am making. 75 dirty paths in the checkout, 25 of them untracked peer work under apps/daemon/src (preview/*, mcp-design-read-query.*); none reverted, stashed or committed. NO file was created or modified by this session.

The failure mode to refuse is writing ANY code, comment, test name or step note here that calls the result atomic. This row stops at a healthy candidate and a recorded receipt.

SECOND — `toMatch(/[0-9a-f]{40}/)` PASSES FOR THE WRONG SHA. DoD-1 says the tag EQUALS the sha VALUE; every later rollback, dossier and incident claim resolves through that tag. Drill (i) is what proves the assertion is a value and not a pattern.

THIRD — THE HEALTH PROBE COULD READ THE CONTAINER IT IS REPLACING. If the probe addresses the environment's public url rather than the candidate by name, it answers 200 from the OLD container and every deploy 'passes' health instantly, making DoD-3 vacuous while green. The plan kills it structurally (`docker inspect ... <candidateName>` — argv that names the candidate) and drill (iii) proves the arm can see it.

FOURTH — THE PIPE IS A SHELL CONSTRUCT AND THERE IS NO SHELL. `docker save | ssh docker load` must be joined in Node, and a pipe hides the first child's exit code by default (`${PIPESTATUS[0]}` is the shell answer, unavailable). Surface BOTH children's failures and assert both argv arrays independently. The adversarial pass adds: what happens to the `ssh` child when `save` dies after `ssh` has started, and does its stdin ever close.

FIFTH — NULL-PAIRING IS A VALIDATOR, NOT A TYPE. `T | null` on both sides merely PERMITS the pairing; the discipline is a decoder that REFUSES both-populated AND neither-populated. Drill (ii) proves it was encoded.

SIXTH — A REFUSAL MUST LEAVE A DEFINED STATE. On `DEPLOY_HEALTH_TIMEOUT` the old container keeps running AND the failed candidate is removed, in a `finally` on the failure path. A half-deployed environment reporting success is worse than a refusal, and so is one reporting a refusal while leaking a stray container. Assert it by reading the double's FINAL STATE, never the return value.

SEVENTH — THE RECEIPT SHAPE AND ITS RETRIEVAL CALL ARE PUBLISHED INTERFACES. task-da60dc4b39c is WORKING NOW and cannot depend on this row. `readPreviousDeployReceipt(store, projectId, environment): DeployReceiptV1 | null` must appear in the completion record with that signature. Do not key the ledger on sha alone — a redeploy of the same sha must not make the previous receipt unreachable.

EIGHTH — THE LAYER CONSTANT NAME CAN DRAG `tests/security/` INTO THIS ROW. See insight 5. A naive `export const DEPLOY_ENGINE_LAYER` at column zero owes a security-roster row plus cardinality pins — foreign files discovered at step 5, past the cap. Name it `DEPLOY_ENGINE_STAMP`.
